name: casemap
algorithm: Lower-case each line of a generated 4 MiB mixed-script text (ASCII, Latin-1, Greek without the sigmas, Cyrillic; splitmix64) with each language's std Unicode case mapping; FNV-1a 64 over the lowered bytes plus their length, wrapping; rounds times (README.md).

skip.c: no std Unicode case mapping in C (tolower maps one byte of the current locale)
skip.zig: no std Unicode case mapping in Zig 0.17 (std.ascii.lowerString maps ASCII only)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; case mapping has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the alphabet leaves out every scalar whose simple and full lower case differ, so every column writes the same bytes, and the hash over them checks every result
notes: Mappings named: mk str.ToLower (simple, one scalar to one), results in an arena reset per round; rust str::to_lowercase (full, context-sensitive; on this alphabet the same as simple), a String per line; go strings.ToLower (simple), a string per line, garbage collected; cs MemoryExtensions.ToLowerInvariant (simple invariant Unicode table, preserved under InvariantGlobalization=true in .NET 11), into a reused char[] buffer per line and encoded to UTF-8 for the checksum. The text is built in the program, once, before the rounds.
Case folding (text.FoldCase) has no cell: no other std here has full case folding (Go's EqualFold is simple folding as a comparison); README.md.
